sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Introduction and Basic Controls: Getting Started in Sakura Town
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: Welcome to Sakura School Simulator, a highly expansive and open-ended sandbox game that places you in the vibrant and unpredictable town of Sakura. As a new player, your very first task is to familiarize yourself with the game's user interface and foundational control mechanics. When you first spawn at your character's house, take a moment to look at your screen and understand the layout. On the bottom left side, you will find the virtual directional joystick, which controls your character's physical movement. Dragging it lightly makes your character walk, while pushing it to the edge allows them to run. Swiping anywhere on the right side of the screen allows you to adjust the camera angle, giving you a full 360-degree view of your surroundings. The primary action buttons are clustered on the bottom right side of the screen. These include dedicated buttons for jumping, attacking, interacting with the environment, and activating your jetpack. The jetpack is perhaps one of the most iconic and incredibly useful tools in Sakura School Simulator, allowing you to traverse the sprawling map quickly, evade danger, and reach hidden areas on rooftops or high mountains. To use it, simply tap the jetpack button, and use your movement joystick to fly around in the air. You also have a dynamic action button that changes its function depending on what object or person you are looking at; for example, if you stand near a door, the action button will allow you to open it, and if you stand near a drivable vehicle, it will prompt you to enter. It is highly recommended to spend your first ten to fifteen minutes simply walking around your starting house, practicing picking up items, sitting on various pieces of furniture, and testing the camera sensitivity. If the game feels too laggy or the controls feel too fast, you can access the system settings menu by tapping the gear icon located in the top left corner of the screen. In this comprehensive menu, you can adjust graphics settings such as shadow quality and draw distance to improve device performance, change the camera movement sensitivity, and even modify the in-game time of day. The game does not hold your hand with a strict tutorial, so mastering these basic movements on your own is absolutely crucial. Additionally, pay close attention to the radar map in the top right corner, which helps you locate important NPCs (Non-Playable Characters), vehicles, objectives, and aggressive enemies. Understanding these foundational mechanics ensures that you are fully prepared for the more complex social interactions, intense combat scenarios, and creative building dynamics you will experience as you finally venture out of your safe house and into the bustling streets of Sakura Town. Remember that there is no right or wrong way to play this game; it is purely driven by your own curiosity and willingness to explore the mechanics.

sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Character Customization and Wardrobe Mastery
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: Character customization is a massive part of the Sakura School Simulator experience, allowing you to express your unique style and even gain special abilities depending on what you wear. Before you even load into the main town, the main menu offers a comprehensive character creation screen where you can select between a male or female protagonist, or even choose to play as a child character. Here, you can adjust fundamental physical traits such as hairstyles, hair color, eye color, and facial expressions. However, the true depth of customization unlocks once you are actually inside the game world. If you navigate to your character's bedroom in their starting house, you will find a glowing pink circle on the floor near the closet. Stepping into this circle opens up the in-game wardrobe menu, providing you with access to dozens of different outfits ranging from traditional Japanese school uniforms and casual streetwear to outlandish costumes like ninja suits, police uniforms, shrine maiden outfits, and even an Alice in Wonderland dress. What many beginners fail to realize is that clothing in Sakura School Simulator is not merely cosmetic; many outfits come with intrinsic stat boosts and unique gameplay mechanics. For example, wearing the Ninja suit fundamentally alters your character's movement animations, allowing you to run much faster, jump incredibly high without needing the jetpack, and throw deadly shurikens as a basic attack. The Alice in Wonderland dress gives you the magical ability to shrink down to a microscopic size or grow into a towering giant, which drastically alters how you interact with the environment and other characters. The police uniform grants you a degree of authority and prevents the local law enforcement from immediately attacking you if you happen to get into a scuffle in town. Furthermore, you can accessorize your character with various items like hats, glasses, masks, and wings. By using the 'Chara Edit' function in the main menu, you can fine-tune the exact positioning, rotation, and scale of these accessories, allowing for truly infinite customization possibilities. You can save your favorite clothing combinations into preset slots, making it easy to switch outfits on the fly without having to return to your house every time. Taking the time to experiment with different outfits not only makes the game visually more enjoyable but also equips you with the necessary tools and abilities to tackle specific missions, defeat tough bosses, or simply cause chaotic fun in the town with your newfound superpowers.

sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Navigating the School: Classes, Clubs, and Activities
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: Despite its wild and unpredictable nature, the core premise of Sakura School Simulator revolves around experiencing the daily life of a high school student. The school itself is a massive, multi-story building located near the center of the map, complete with classrooms, a cafeteria, a massive gymnasium, an outdoor track, and various club rooms. If you wish to play the game as a peaceful life simulator, attending school is highly rewarding. The in-game clock dictates the school schedule. Classes typically begin in the morning around 8:30 AM. If you walk into your designated classroom and sit at your assigned desk, your character will automatically begin taking notes. Attending these classes is not just for roleplaying purposes; sitting through a lesson actually increases your character's intelligence stat, which can unlock specific dialogue options and improve your overall standing with the teachers. Each classroom focuses on a different subject, such as mathematics, literature, or science, and you can freely wander the halls to explore them all. When the lunch bell rings, the school becomes bustling with activity as NPC students flood the hallways. You can visit the cafeteria to purchase various foods and drinks, which restore your character's hunger and health meters. Buying food for other students is also a fantastic way to quickly build friendships. After standard classes conclude in the afternoon, club activities begin. The school offers several extracurricular clubs that you can join, each providing unique benefits and interactive props. For instance, joining the martial arts club allows you to practice your combat skills on training dummies and learn new hand-to-hand fighting techniques. The archery club provides you with a bow and arrow, letting you practice your marksmanship on targets. The brass band club lets you pick up various musical instruments that actually produce sound when interacted with. You can also visit the swimming pool or the track field to increase your physical strength and stamina stats. Interacting with the teachers is another crucial aspect of school life; being polite and attending their classes will make them like you, whereas causing trouble, attacking students, or bringing weapons onto the campus will prompt the teachers to chase you down or call the police. Balancing your academic life with the sheer chaos of the town outside is a fun challenge, and fully exploring the massive school building will reveal numerous hidden items, secret rooms, and interesting NPC behaviors that bring the simulated environment to life.

sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Making Friends and Building Relationships
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: One of the most complex and engaging systems in Sakura School Simulator is the social and relationship mechanic. The town of Sakura is populated by dozens of unique NPCs, ranging from fellow students and teachers to shopkeepers, yakuza members, and ordinary citizens. You can interact with almost every single person you meet, and building relationships with them can drastically alter your gameplay experience. When you approach an NPC, an 'Interact' or 'Talk' button will appear. Tapping this opens up a dialogue menu with several options. The most basic way to increase an NPC's affection towards you is by using the 'Compliment' option. Constantly praising a character will slowly raise their relationship meter, moving their status from a mere acquaintance to a friend, a close friend, and eventually a lover. However, words alone will only get you so far. To significantly boost a relationship, you need to give gifts. You can purchase flowers from the local flower shop, or buy various foods and cakes from the convenience store or bakery to hand out. Giving a character their favorite item will result in a massive affection boost. As your relationship with an NPC improves, you unlock new interaction options. Friends can be asked to 'Follow Me,' meaning they will run behind you wherever you go, effectively acting as your companions or bodyguards. If you give a weapon to a follower, they will actively help you fight enemies during combat scenarios. When a relationship reaches the 'Lover' status, you unlock romantic interactions such as hugging and kissing. The game also features a mood system; NPCs can become angry, sad, or happy based on how you treat them and what happens around them. If you accidentally hit an NPC or insult them, their affection will plummet, and they may either run away in fear or become hostile and attack you. If you make enemies, they will hold a grudge and attack you on sight the next time they see you. Interestingly, you can also use special items like 'Love Potions,' which can be bought or found hidden in the world, to instantly make an NPC fall in love with you regardless of your previous interactions. Building a loyal group of friends and followers is highly recommended before tackling some of the game's harder boss fights, as having a small army of armed students watching your back can turn an impossible battle into an easy victory.

sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Combat Mechanics: Weapons, Fighting, and Self-Defense
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: While Sakura School Simulator can be played peacefully, it also boasts a surprisingly robust and chaotic combat system. Whether you are defending yourself from angry students, fighting off the local Yakuza, or battling giant aliens, understanding how to fight is absolutely essential. Combat in the game is divided into two main categories: melee (hand-to-hand) and ranged (firearms). At the start of the game, your character can punch and kick using the primary attack button. However, unarmed combat is relatively weak and should only be used as a last resort. To truly become formidable, you need to acquire weapons. One of the easiest ways to get early-game weapons is to visit the Yakuza Office located on the map. Sneaking into their compound (or aggressively fighting your way through) will grant you access to powerful weapons like katanas, pistols, assault rifles, shotguns, and even rocket launchers. Once you have a weapon equipped, your attack button changes to reflect the item. For firearms, a crosshair will appear on the screen. The game features a soft lock-on system; if you face the general direction of an enemy, your shots will automatically track them to a certain degree, making mobile combat much easier. Managing ammo is critical, as guns will run out of bullets. You can purchase more ammunition from the harbor or find it scattered in hidden locations. Movement during combat is key to survival. Utilizing the jetpack while shooting allows you to rain down fire from above while avoiding enemy melee attacks. You can also use the dash button to quickly dodge incoming projectiles. It is important to note the game's unique health and damage mechanics. When you deplete an enemy's health bar, they do not die; instead, they 'faint' and fall to the ground with swirling stars above their heads. This maintains the somewhat lighthearted tone of the game. However, actions have consequences. If you attack innocent civilians or start fights in the middle of town, witnesses will run to call the police. Once the police are alerted, officers armed with pistols will spawn and hunt you down relentlessly. Fighting the police only increases your wanted level, causing more officers to appear. To lose the police, you can try flying away, hiding inside buildings, or changing your clothes to reset your status. Mastering combat requires balancing aggression with tactical movement and knowing when it is smarter to simply fly away.

sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Exploring the Town: Vehicles, Fast Travel, and Hidden Locations
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: The town of Sakura is massive, featuring diverse environments ranging from dense urban streets and residential neighborhoods to quiet mountain shrines, amusement parks, and secret underground facilities. Exploring every inch of this map is one of the most rewarding aspects of the game, and doing so on foot would take hours. Thankfully, the game provides several methods of transportation. Right outside your starting house, you will find a personal car and a bicycle. Walking up to a vehicle and pressing the action button allows you to enter the driver's seat. Driving mechanics feature an accelerator, a brake/reverse pedal, and directional steering arrows. Driving is a fantastic way to cover ground quickly, but you must be careful; vehicles in Sakura School Simulator have a durability system. If you crash into walls, other cars, or NPCs too many times, the car will begin to smoke, catch fire, and eventually become completely disabled. If your car is destroyed, you can take it to the local Repair Shop (located near the gas station) to have it fixed for a small monetary fee. Beyond your personal vehicles, you can essentially 'borrow' or hijack almost any vehicle you see on the street, including sports cars, delivery trucks, and police cruisers. For those who want to skip the travel time entirely, the game features a highly convenient Fast Travel system. By tapping the 'Menu' button in the top left corner, you are presented with a comprehensive list of major locations in the town. Tapping any of these names—such as the School, Hospital, Amusement Park, Shrine, or Yakuza Office—will instantly teleport you to that location. This is incredibly useful for escaping dangerous situations or completing time-sensitive missions. As you explore, you will discover that Sakura town is filled with hidden locations that are not immediately obvious on the main map. For example, diving into the waterways might lead you to hidden sewer tunnels, flying high above the ocean will reveal a secret remote island, and investigating the school at night might uncover haunted areas. The Amusement Park features fully functional rides like a rollercoaster, a Ferris wheel, and teacups that you can actually ride. The Hospital allows you to buy medical supplies or heal yourself if your health is low. Taking the time to manually explore the map using your jetpack or a fast car will constantly reward you with hidden money, secret weapons, and bizarre easter eggs scattered throughout the environment.

sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Earning and Spending Money: Jobs and Shops
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: Money is a vital resource in Sakura School Simulator, required for purchasing food, buying gifts for NPCs, acquiring ammunition, paying for vehicle repairs, and buying special consumable items. Unlike many other games, you do not start with a massive bank account, so learning how to generate income is a crucial early-game objective. There are several ways to earn Yen in Sakura town. The most direct method for beginners is simply finding it scattered around the map. If you look carefully inside your character's house, on the roofs of buildings, inside the school, and hidden in alleyways, you will find floating stacks of Yen that you can simply walk over to collect. Another interesting way to get money is by asking for it. If you build a high enough relationship with certain NPCs (especially wealthy ones), you can use the dialogue menu to literally ask them for money, and they will occasionally hand over a significant amount. However, for a more reliable and immersive income stream, you can take on part-time jobs. For example, if you visit the auto repair shop, you can put on a mechanic's uniform and work there to earn a steady paycheck. Similarly, you can work at the local cafe or the sushi restaurant, serving customers and earning money for your time. Once you have accumulated a healthy amount of Yen, you need to know where to spend it. The town is filled with various functional shops. The Convenience Store (Mart) and the Bakery are your go-to locations for buying food and drinks. Consuming these items restores your hunger meter, which naturally depletes over time, and regenerates your health if you have taken damage in combat. The Flower Shop is essential for buying bouquets to woo potential romantic partners. At the harbor, you can find a somewhat hidden merchant who sells heavy weaponry and ammunition, which requires a substantial amount of money. You can also purchase whimsical and powerful items like the 'Love Potion,' which instantly maxes out an NPC's affection, or shrinking and growing potions. If your vehicle is damaged, a large portion of your funds will go to the repair shop to make it drivable again. Understanding the game's simple but effective economy ensures that you are always well-stocked on healing items, heavily armed for boss fights, and financially capable of making any NPC in town fall in love with you.

sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Quests and Missions: Completing Objectives
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: While a large portion of Sakura School Simulator is dedicated to unguided sandbox fun, the game does feature a structured mission system for players who want specific goals and challenges to complete. To access your current objectives, tap on the trophy icon or navigate to the 'Missions' tab in your main menu. Here, you will find a long list of tasks ranging from incredibly simple daily activities to highly complex, multi-stage combat encounters. Some of the simpler missions include attending a specific class at school, buying a certain item from a shop, or making a new friend. These act as a soft tutorial, encouraging you to engage with the game's various mechanics. However, the mission list also contains much more bizarre and dangerous tasks. For example, one mission requires you to defeat the leader of the Yakuza, forcing you to infiltrate their heavily guarded compound, fight through dozens of armed gangsters, and survive a tough boss battle. Other missions are heavily time-dependent. The game features an internal clock, and certain events only trigger at specific times of the day. One famous mission tasks you with defeating the UFOs that only appear in the sky during the late evening. Another requires you to go to the school's science lab at exactly midnight, where you will be ambushed by animated, hostile skeletal models. Tracking your progress is simple, as the mission menu will cross off tasks as you complete them, and you will often be rewarded with large sums of money or unique items for your efforts. Because the game allows you to manipulate time via the settings menu, you do not have to wait around in real-time to trigger these specific events; you can simply fast-forward the clock to night time to immediately start the UFO or haunted school missions. It is important to read the mission descriptions carefully, as some require you to wear specific clothing or be in a certain location to trigger the event. If you manage to complete all the missions, or if you simply want to experience them again, the game allows you to reset your mission progress from the settings, providing endless replayability. Engaging with the mission system provides a sense of direction and structure to the otherwise chaotic sandbox, giving you a reason to fully utilize the combat, relationship, and exploration mechanics you have mastered.

sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Building and Props: Using the Base Building System
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: One of the most powerful, creative, and often overlooked features in Sakura School Simulator is the 'Item Edit' and prop-building system. This feature effectively turns the game from a standard life simulator into a fully-fledged 3D sandbox builder, allowing you to construct your own houses, create custom obstacle courses, or entirely redesign the landscape of the town. To access this mode, open the main menu and select the 'Chara Edit / Item Edit' button, then navigate to the 'Item' and 'Props' tabs. Here, you are presented with a massive catalog of spawnable objects, categorized into building materials (walls, floors, stairs, roofs), furniture (beds, chairs, tables, TVs), nature items (trees, rocks, flowers), and various miscellaneous objects (ramps, geometric shapes, interactive electronics). Once you select an item, it will spawn directly in front of your character. The true power of this system lies in the manipulation tools provided on the right side of the screen. You can use the X, Y, and Z axis buttons to perfectly position the item anywhere in the world. You can rotate the item to any angle, and most importantly, you can scale it to make it massively larger or microscopically smaller. This means a simple wooden plank can be scaled up to serve as a massive bridge between two buildings. The physics engine interacts with these props in real-time, meaning you can build ramps to launch your cars off of, or create barricades to protect yourself from the police. You can even change the color and material texture of most objects, turning a standard brick wall into glowing glass or solid gold. Building an entire custom mansion from scratch is entirely possible and highly encouraged by the community. Because building complex structures takes a significant amount of time, the game kindly provides a saving system specifically for your props. You can save your custom creations into different data slots, ensuring that your hard work is not lost when you close the app. When you reload the game, simply load your saved prop data, and your custom house or obstacle course will instantly reappear in the world exactly where you left it. Mastering the prop system unleashes limitless creative potential, allowing you to effectively design your own mini-games and custom environments within the Sakura universe.

sakura_school_simulator_guide.title: Secrets, Easter Eggs, and Boss Fights
sakura_school_simulator_guide.text: Once you have mastered the controls, made friends, built custom houses, and earned plenty of money, it is time to uncover the deep secrets, hidden lore, and challenging boss fights that Sakura School Simulator has tucked away in its strangest corners. The developers have packed the map with numerous bizarre easter eggs that reward adventurous players. For instance, if you visit the local Shinto Shrine, you will find a small cat NPC. Interacting with the shrine allows you to purchase various buffs, but more importantly, it provides the ability to 'revive' any NPCs who have fainted in combat, ensuring that you don't permanently lose your favorite characters. The town is also heavily populated with hidden bosses that offer the ultimate combat challenge. We previously mentioned the UFOs that invade at night and the haunted skeletons in the school, but there is much more. If you venture out to the remote island in the ocean, you may encounter giant, hostile characters. If you explore the underground sewer system, you will find hidden gold and strange enemies lurking in the dark. One of the most famous secrets involves the giant statues located near the shrine and the school; under specific conditions, or by using weapons to agitate them, these massive stone figures will come to life and aggressively attack you, requiring heavy weaponry and intense jetpack maneuvering to defeat. Additionally, the game features a giant bear costume boss and various Yakuza hit squads that require strategic planning to overcome. Many of these secrets are tied to specific outfits or items. For example, using the Alice in Wonderland dress to shrink yourself allows you to enter tiny, otherwise inaccessible mouse holes scattered around certain buildings, revealing miniature secret rooms. The game rarely tells you where these secrets are, encouraging a community-driven approach where players share their findings online. Don't be afraid to poke around behind buildings, fly to the highest skyboxes, dive to the bottom of the ocean, or attack seemingly inanimate objects to see what happens. Sakura School Simulator is designed to be a playground of absurdity, and the more you push the boundaries of its physics and mechanics, the more hidden boss fights, secret weapons, and hilarious easter eggs you will discover to keep your gameplay experience fresh and exciting for months to come.
